declared.title: Does mental contrasting with implementation intentions (MCII) help to increase physical activity?
declared.foundIn: reports/choose-your-struggle/counter-evidence.md (card 11); Crossref search « Kędra Łaguna MCII online intervention randomized Current Issues in Personality Psychology » (2026-11-26)

population: two online trials in Poland with active people: 59 students aiming to walk more, 112 gym-goers without a coach aiming at more aerobic training

findings.text: An online MCII exercise had no significant effect on physical activity, self-efficacy or engagement over two weeks, in either trial, against a short text on the value of activity (power computed for a medium effect only)

support.sentence: No statistically significant effects of the MCII online intervention were observed in either Study 1 or Study 2.

limits: small samples (59 and 112), two weeks of follow-up; power computed for a medium effect (f = 0.25): a small effect is not excluded; effect sizes in a supplement (not read)
activity copied by participants from a phone app (steps, study 1) or self-reported in a calendar (aerobic minutes, study 2)
control: a short text on the importance of physical activity, also read by the MCII group: close to doing nothing, no wish or image of the result
people already active: little room to improve; in study 1, 60 of 242 eligible people filled in the first questionnaire
independent of the creators of MCII; Poland, in Polish; no sample from the Middle East or North Africa
